transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well… it’s mostly when I get into a slow elevator, or a little room where the door’s locked. My chest kind of jumps right away, and I just feel like I need to get out before I can think much about it.
Do you get this same fear in other places besides elevators or locked rooms?

Mostly places like that, yeah. A small storage room maybe, or places with no window… if the door shuts tight, my mind kind of treats it like trouble, even if I know it’s not really the same as being locked up.
Have you ever had one of these sudden fear attacks when you were not in a small or closed-in place?
Not really… it seems to hit when I’m in those closed-in places. Like a slow elevator or a small locked room—then it comes on right away.
When you’re in one of those places, is the main fear that you won’t be able to get out?
Yeah… mostly. I know an elevator or a little storage room isn’t really like being locked in somewhere, but once there’s no window and the door shuts tight, my mind just takes it that way.
Besides elevators or small locked rooms, do you also feel this fear in open public places like crowds or on buses?

No… not really crowds or buses. It’s more when it’s shut in, like an elevator or a little room with no window and the door tight. I know it’s not the same as being locked up, but my mind kind of treats it that way.
When you’re not in an enclosed place, do you worry about having one of these attacks out of the blue?
No… I don’t really sit around worrying it’ll happen out of nowhere. It’s when I step into a slow elevator or a small locked room—then it hits right away, and I just want to get back out.
